title: VPC Replay Operator for Reproducible Customer Workloads
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Build an operator and accompanying harness to reliably replay customer workloads inside Private/VPC/on-prem environments for performance benchmarking and regression detection. The operator should provision a workload controller that can: 1) snapshot request traces and environment metadata from a customer session, 2) replay traffic with network shaping, header injection, and KV-cache priming, and 3) produce reproducible tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency distributions, and regression alerts that map back to model/runtime changes. This is intended for reproducing customer-reported performance regressions and for continuous benchmarking against release branches.
acceptance_criteria: Operator deploys via Helm/manifest into customer VPC with RBAC-limited service account
Workload snapshot format (JSONL) captures request shape, sequence lengths, KV cache warmup steps, env vars, and model version
Replay runs reproduce tokens/sec within ±10% and p95 within ±15% of original captured run for at least 3 separate customer traces
Automated regression detector emits alerts when p95 increases >10% or token/sec drops >15% compared to baseline run
Artifact links (raw traces, replay logs, perf histograms) uploaded to secure S3 and linked from the ticket
Runs wire up to Grafana dashboard and regression CI job that can be run against a candidate runtime image
design_notes: We avoid full VM snapshotting to keep footprint small; instead capture deterministic workload artifacts and env diffs
Trade-off: network shaping will emulate latency/jitter but cannot perfectly reproduce noisy shared infra — document variance expectations
Use a two-phase replay: priming phase (KV cache + prefix tokens) then steady-state phase (continuous traffic) to measure tokens/sec and steady p95
Prefer eBPF-based tracing where available to reduce probe-induced variance; fallback to agent-based capture in strict on-prem installs
implementation_plan: MVP operator: CRD for ReplayJob, controller to spin up replay pods with mounted snapshot artifacts
Replay toolkit: workload player with configurable rate, concurrency, header overrides, and KV priming hooks
Instrumentation: histogram buckets for p50/p95/p99, token counters, GPU utilization exporter, and wall-clock throughput
Regression detector service: ingest baseline + current run metrics, compute relative deltas, generate GitHub issue or Slack alert
CI integration: add workflow that runs replay against runtime-branch images in a dedicated infra project and fails on regression rules
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Rao: Created ticket after on-call incident where customer reported sudden p95 regression only in their VPC. Captured initial trace and sketch of Snapshot format. See Confluence draft.

2026-03-07 - Marco Chen: Prototype operator that accepts a ReplayJob CRD and launches a replay pod. Initial runs show tokens/sec variance of ~22% vs captured trace — likely due to missing KV priming step. PR opened: #412.
2026-03-09 - Priya Mehta (SRE): Reviewed operator security posture. Requested node affinity options and explicit S3 presigned access to avoid long-lived credentials.

2026-03-11 - Marco Chen: Added KV priming and two-phase replay. After priming, tokens/sec variance dropped to ~8% and p95 delta to ~12% for first customer trace. Still seeing differences on noisy multi-tenant hosts.
2026-03-12 - Design review (Ethan Park): Suggested adding deterministic RNG seeding for request ordering to increase reproducibility across runs. Approved design change.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Rao: Added regression detector prototype. Next steps: wire up to CI and add dashboard panels for per-run deltas. Need security review for S3 storage policy.
qa_notes: Use three distinct customer traces (short, medium, long seq) for validation
Run each replay 5x and compute median/variance; require stable baselines before enabling automatic regression alerts
Record environment diffs including kernel version, CUDA driver, and instance type in replay metadata
